name: plain-vs-rag-primary-v1
arm_a: plain LLM (plain-v2 prompt, no repository evidence)
arm_b: repository-aware RAG (rag-v1 prompt, original line retriever, top-k 5)
retriever_rationale: The original line-window retriever (60 lines, 10 overlap, 512 tokens; Jina v2 base code, prefixed text, FAISS IndexFlatIP, top-k 5) is the one the project's earlier answers and the 8192-token historical run used. Milestones 5b and 10 compared retrieval variants on retrieval metrics; they did not establish that any variant yields better *answers*, so no superiority is claimed here and no variant was tuned on this benchmark. Using the original retriever also keeps the eight verified historical RAG responses comparable.
held_equal: the question text (one field, sent verbatim to both arms)
prompt_fairness: plain-v1 had no abstention or labelling instruction while rag-v1 does, which would confound the comparison; plain-v2 adds the same honesty rules (do not state repository specifics you cannot know, label repository evidence vs general knowledge, say explicitly when you cannot answer) without any evidence. Residual asymmetry: only RAG is told to cite [Source n]. plain-v1 and rag-v1 are unchanged and pinned by SHA-256.

primary_endpoint.name: paired difference in mean key-fact correctness (RAG - plain), answerable questions
primary_endpoint.definition: For every answerable question both arms answered successfully and that were judged successfully, d = score(RAG) - score(plain) where score is the 0-2 key-fact correctness score of rubric gen-rubric-1. The estimate is the mean of d, with a percentile bootstrap 95% CI over questions (shared resample indices, fixed seed). Reported per repository and combined. Questions with a missing or failed side are listed and counted separately, never dropped silently and never imputed. A claim of improvement requires the CI to exclude 0; the synthetic and the self-referential repository are not pooled into a single headline without also showing each one.

secondary_endpoints.name: completeness
secondary_endpoints.definition: Fraction of key facts judged supported.

secondary_endpoints.name: citation correctness
secondary_endpoints.definition: Programmatic: fraction of the answer's citations that resolve to a real file and line range (valid_fraction); applicable to RAG, and to plain answers only when they write explicit file:line locations. Never imputed for answers without citations.

secondary_endpoints.name: hallucinated-reference indicators
secondary_endpoints.definition: Programmatic and conservative: count of repository files/symbols named in an answer that do not exist in the frozen repository (not_found), per answer; ambiguous/cannot-evaluate reported separately.

secondary_endpoints.name: appropriate abstention
secondary_endpoints.definition: Unanswerable questions: share of responses that abstain (system or text).

secondary_endpoints.name: false refusal
secondary_endpoints.definition: Answerable questions: share of responses that refuse or say evidence is insufficient.

secondary_endpoints.name: retrieval relevance
secondary_endpoints.definition: RAG only: whether a retrieved source overlaps a key-fact region (hit@k).

secondary_endpoints.name: latency
secondary_endpoints.definition: Wall-clock seconds of generated sides only (cache hits and reused historical responses are excluded and counted).

secondary_endpoints.name: tokens
secondary_endpoints.definition: Input, output and reasoning tokens reported by the provider (when reported).

secondary_endpoints.name: end-to-end reliability
secondary_endpoints.definition: Share of requested sides that ended successful / failed / not attempted.

judge.note: Blind to the arm; a different model family from the generator is recommended.

limitations: The copilot repository was authored by the project team and its documentation is in the retrieval index: this arm measures retrieval-augmented use of a repository the model has probably never seen, but the question author knew the code (author bias).
The second repository is synthetic and written by the project team: it tests mechanics on unseen code, not performance on real-world independent software.
A single hosted model generates both arms; results do not transfer to other models.
The rubric judge is an LLM and is validated only through a human audit of a ~20% sample; judge self-preference toward the generator's model family is possible.
Plain-v2 receives the same honesty rules as RAG but cannot cite [Source n]; citation metrics are therefore RAG-only unless the plain answer writes explicit locations.
